tagline: Wahi HTTP, TLS mein sealed, taaki raaste mein koi use padh na sake.
description: HTTPS aam HTTP hi hai jo TLS connection ke andar carry hota hai. TLS 1.3 ek round trip mein fresh keys par agree hota hai, certificate se server ki identity prove karta hai, aur phir har request aur response ko encrypt karta hai. Padlock ka matlab hai ki teeno cheezein kaam kar gayi.

normal.name: https://example.com kholna
normal.summary: TCP, ek-round-trip TLS 1.3 handshake, phir encrypted request aur response.

steps.title: Port 443 par TCP
steps.detail: HTTPS ab bhi TCP par chalta hai. Browser port 443 se connect karta hai, jo standard HTTPS port hai. Abhi kuch encrypted nahi hai; woh agle step mein aata hai.

steps.title: Client Hello
steps.desc: Ciphers, site ka naam aur key share
steps.detail: Browser sab kuch ek saath bhejta hai: jo cipher suites woh support karta hai, jo site chahiye (SNI), jo versions woh bolta hai, aur ek fresh x25519 key exchange ka apna hissa. Key share pehle hi bhej dena hi wajah hai ki TLS 1.3 ko sirf ek round trip chahiye.

quiz.q: Café Wi-Fi par koi sniffing kar raha hai aur use yeh packet dikhta hai. Woh kya seekh sakta hai?
options: Site ka naam example.com, lekin page ya data nahi
quiz.why: Client Hello ka SNI clear mein bheja jaata hai. Paths, headers aur bodies baad mein aate hain aur encrypted hote hain.

steps.title: Server Hello + certificate
steps.desc: Keys agree ho gayi; baaki sab pehle se encrypted
steps.detail: Server ek cipher chunta hai aur Server Hello mein apna key share bhejta hai. Ab dono sides same secret compute kar leti hain. Uske baad sab kuch encrypted hai: server ka certificate, uska signature jo prove karta hai ki certificate usi ka hai, aur uska Finished message. Yeh ek segment ke liye bahut bada hai, isliye do mein aata hai.

quiz.q: TLS 1.3 mein kya eavesdropper server ka certificate padh sakta hai?
options: Haan, woh hamesha clear mein bheja jaata hai
Nahi, woh handshake keys se encrypted hota hai
Sirf agar server RSA use kare
quiz.why: TLS 1.3 Server Hello ke baad sab kuch encrypt karta hai, certificate samet. TLS 1.2 mein woh dikhta tha.

steps.title: Certificate check karo
steps.desc: Kya yeh sach mein example.com hai?
steps.detail: Browser certificate decrypt karke teen cheezein check karta hai: naam example.com se match karta hai, expire nahi hua, aur signatures ki chain ek aise root authority tak jaati hai jispar browser bharosa karta hai. Woh server ka signature bhi check karta hai, jo prove karta hai ki server ke paas private key hai. Phir woh apna Finished bhejta hai.
facts: Must end at a trusted root

quiz.q: Agar certificate kisi aur naam ka hota to kya hota?
options: Browser certificate error ke saath ruk jaata
TLS 1.2 par fall back ho jaata
quiz.why: Naam mismatch ka matlab hai browser pakka nahi kar sakta ki woh kisse baat kar raha hai, isliye woh aage badhne se mana kar deta hai.

steps.title: Encrypted request
steps.desc: GET / Application Data ke roop mein jaata hai
steps.detail: Ab browser apni request bhejta hai. Wire par yeh bas random dikhne wale bytes ka Application Data record hai. Andar GET / apne saare headers aur cookies ke saath hai, jise raaste mein koi bhi na padh sakta hai na badal sakta hai bina tag check fail hue.

steps.title: Encrypted response
steps.detail: Server pehle do session tickets bhejta hai jinhe browser baad mein tezi se reconnect karne ke liye use kar sakta hai, phir page ke saath 200 OK response. Sab kuch encrypted hai. Response headers mein Strict-Transport-Security hai, jo wire par dikhta nahi lekin ab browser use yaad rakhta hai.

steps.title: Padlock aur HSTS
steps.detail: Page padlock ke saath dikhta hai. Header Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains ki wajah se, agle ek saal browser koi bhi http://example.com link kuch bhejne se pehle https:// bana dega, aur tumhe certificate errors ke paar click karne nahi dega.

quiz.q: Agle hafte tum http://example.com type karte ho. Browser pehle kya bhejta hai?
options: Tumhare confirm karne tak kuch nahi
quiz.why: HSTS browser ko URL ko internally https:// mein badalne par majboor karta hai, isliye laptop se koi plain request kabhi nikalti hi nahi.

outro.title: Private aur proven
outro.text: TCP connect hua, TLS 1.3 ne ek round trip mein keys agree ki, certificate ne prove kiya ki server example.com hai, aur uske baad har HTTP byte encrypted tha. HSTS ensure karta hai ki aage ki visits plain HTTP ko poori tarah skip karein.

mitm.name: Café Wi-Fi par man in the middle
mitm.summary: Wahi Wi-Fi par ek attacker connection intercept karke fake certificate dikhata hai. Browser mana kar deta hai.

steps.title: Traffic hijack hota hai
steps.desc: ARP spoofing packets attacker ko bhejti hai
steps.detail: Café Wi-Fi par attacker fake ARP replies se laptop ko bolta hai "main router hoon". Ab laptop ke frames attacker ke MAC address par jaate hain, bhale andar ka IP address abhi bhi 203.0.113.10 kehta hai. Attacker server ban kar TCP handshake ka jawab deta hai.

quiz.q: Kya laptop TCP handshake se jaan sakta hai ki kuch galat hai?
options: Nahi, TCP mein prove karne ka koi tarika nahi ki jawab kisne diya
quiz.why: TCP aur IP identity ka koi proof carry nahi karte. Raaste mein koi bhi jawab de sakta hai. Woh proof TLS ka kaam hai.

steps.title: Attacker ko Client Hello
steps.detail: Bekhabar browser apna normal Client Hello bhejta hai. Attacker SNI padhta hai aur jaan jaata hai ki victim example.com chahta hai. Traffic padhne ke liye ab use example.com banne ka natak karna padega.

steps.title: Fake certificate
steps.desc: Khud banaya hua, trusted authority ne sign nahi kiya
steps.detail: Attacker apne key share ke saath key exchange poora karta hai, isliye woh laptop ka bheja hua decrypt kar sakta hai. Lekin use example.com ka certificate bhi bhejna hai, aur koi trusted authority use woh issue nahi karegi. Woh apna khud sign kiya hua certificate bhejta hai.

quiz.q: Attacker example.com ka asli certificate copy kyun nahi kar leta?
options: Handshake sign karne ke liye use asli server ki private key bhi chahiye
Certificates har minute expire hote hain
Browser use cache kar leta hai
quiz.why: Certificate public hota hai. CertificateVerify signature ke liye matching private key chahiye, jo sirf asli server ke paas hai.

steps.title: Browser use block kar deta hai
steps.detail: Browser is certificate se kisi bhi trusted root tak chain nahi bana paata. Woh ek encrypted alert (unknown_ca) bhejta hai aur connection drop kar deta hai. Koi HTTP request kabhi bheji hi nahi gayi, isliye koi cookies ya passwords leak nahi hue. Kyunki example.com HSTS use karta hai, warning page par "proceed anyway" button hota hi nahi.

outro.title: Certificate ne attack roka
outro.text: Attacker packets intercept kar sakta tha aur key exchange bhi poora kar sakta tha, lekin woh prove nahi kar saka ki woh example.com hai. Certificate checks ek chhupi interception ko zor ke error mein badal dete hain, aur HSTS woh button hata deta hai jo users ko jaal mein jaane deta hai.
facts: Certificate chain to a trusted root

cheatsheet.title: TLS 1.3 handshake
items: Dono sides handshake confirm karti hain
